operations.title: Train a steering vector
operations.purpose: Teach a vector to favor a chosen answer over an alternative, while preserving other judgments and abilities. Start with your own choice prompts or prompts prepared from study outputs.

fields.label: Model to execute
fields.help: Choose the prepared model; this does not acquire weights.

fields.label: Model commit
fields.help: The exact version of the model. Inspect the selected model to fill its commit automatically; an agent can also supply a verified commit. This prevents silently switching model versions.

fields.label: Injection layer
fields.help: The transformer layer where the learned vector is added (zero-based). Choose a layer supported by your model and study design; no universal best layer is assumed.

fields.label: Dose in residual-norm units
fields.help: Steering strength relative to the model’s typical activation size. For example, 0.1 means one tenth of the measured residual norm. This is not a J-space artifact-norm multiple.

fields.label: Artifact supplying the residual norm
fields.help: Choose an inspected artifact with a residual norm table, or explicitly provide alphaAbsolute under advanced settings.

fields.label: Target training items
fields.help: Examples of the behavior to change. For each prompt, state two answer choices and the answer to encourage. Training increases its log-probability relative to the other choice. Study outputs must first be authored into this choice-row format; they are not consumed directly. Use one JSON object per line (.jsonl), with distinct item IDs across splits. The example below illustrates syntax only; it is not a ready-made research dataset.
fields.example: {"id": "example-1", "prompt": "A box contains two red balls and one blue ball. Which color is more common? A: red. B: blue. Answer A or B.", "options": ["A", "B"], "target": "A"}

fields.label: Selection / validation items
fields.help: Separate examples of the same behavior, used for checkpoint selection or monitoring. Do not reuse training or final-test rows. A declared fixed-step run can omit this file. Use one JSON object per line (.jsonl), with distinct item IDs across splits. The example below illustrates syntax only; it is not a ready-made research dataset.
fields.example: {"id": "example-1", "prompt": "A box contains two red balls and one blue ball. Which color is more common? A: red. B: blue. Answer A or B.", "options": ["A", "B"], "target": "A"}

fields.label: Behaviors to preserve
fields.help: Judgments you want to leave unchanged. The optimizer penalizes changes to the unsteered model’s answer probabilities on these prompts, rather than teaching the target label as a new answer. Use one JSON object per line (.jsonl), with distinct item IDs across splits. The example below illustrates syntax only; it is not a ready-made research dataset.
fields.example: {"id": "example-1", "prompt": "A box contains two red balls and one blue ball. Which color is more common? A: red. B: blue. Answer A or B.", "options": ["A", "B"], "target": "A"}

fields.label: Anchor validation items
fields.help: Separate preservation examples for checking whether the trained vector changes judgments you meant to preserve. Keep them distinct from the preservation training rows. Use one JSON object per line (.jsonl), with distinct item IDs across splits. The example below illustrates syntax only; it is not a ready-made research dataset.
fields.example: {"id": "example-1", "prompt": "A box contains two red balls and one blue ball. Which color is more common? A: red. B: blue. Answer A or B.", "options": ["A", "B"], "target": "A"}

fields.label: Capability training controls
fields.help: Questions with objectively correct answers, such as basic reasoning or factual tasks. Here target is the correct answer; the optimizer penalizes losing it. Use examples relevant to the abilities your study needs. Use one JSON object per line (.jsonl), with distinct item IDs across splits. The example below illustrates syntax only; it is not a ready-made research dataset.
fields.example: {"id": "example-1", "prompt": "A box contains two red balls and one blue ball. Which color is more common? A: red. B: blue. Answer A or B.", "options": ["A", "B"], "target": "A"}

fields.label: Maximum optimization steps
fields.help: Upper limit on optimizer updates, not the number of examples. The existing default is a starting setting to review, not a recommended value for every study.

fields.label: Random seed
fields.help: Record the seed before execution.

fields.label: Name for this reading
fields.help: A new immutable result will be created.

questions: What behavior should change, and in which direction?

operations.title: Fit a new J-lens
operations.purpose: Build a model-specific instrument that maps intermediate residual activations into the final-layer basis. Choose your text, measure a pilot, and retain the fitting recipe.

fields.label: Model to fit
fields.help: Choose a prepared Hugging Face checkpoint. Fitting does not download model weights or change them.

fields.label: Exact model version
fields.help: Inspect the model to pin its 40-character commit. The resulting lens belongs to this checkpoint.

fields.label: Text corpus for fitting
fields.help: Use varied text representative of where you intend to read the model. This is not positive/negative concept data. Supply UTF-8 JSONL with one unique id and text per row. Choose existing text, or ask for an authoring prompt; no data is generated automatically.
fields.example: {"id":"sample-1","text":"Replace this sentence with a sufficiently long passage from your chosen, documented corpus."}

fields.label: Corpus preparation receipt
fields.help: Optional preparation.json saved beside a prepared corpus. It records source revisions, selected records, sampling, and token review, and travels with the fitting inputs. Existing manually authored corpora do not need a receipt.

fields.label: Maximum corpus rows (start with a small pilot)
fields.help: Fits the first N rows in file order. Four rows provide a timing pilot, not a well-established lens. Increase after reviewing time, memory, and corpus coverage. Short rows are counted in this limit and recorded as skipped. The request review shows matrix memory and backward-pass estimates when the pinned model configuration is cached locally; otherwise it explains how to obtain an engine estimate.

fields.label: Source layers
fields.help: Blank fits all layers before the final block. Select fewer layers for a cheaper or targeted instrument; token-vector creation needs full coverage. Layer numbers start at zero.

fields.label: Maximum tokens per passage
fields.help: Longer text is truncated to this many tokens. Raw text uses the tokenizer’s native special tokens; no chat template is added.

fields.label: Leading token positions to omit
fields.help: The reference estimator omits early positions and the final token. A passage must have more than this value plus one token after tokenization.

fields.label: Jacobian dimensions per backward pass
fields.help: A memory/performance control. The model repeats the passage this many times per pass. Larger values need more activation memory; start with 1 on a large model. For example, width 5,376 needs 5,376 backward passes per row at batch 1, or 672 at batch 8. Batching uses more activation memory; it does not promise proportional acceleration.

fields.label: Checkpoint every N considered rows
fields.help: A checkpoint may contain several gigabytes. Smaller intervals preserve more progress but increase disk traffic. Active scratch keeps the latest complete snapshot; completed runs retain their final snapshot.

fields.label: Model precision
fields.help: Choose bfloat16, float32, or float16. The fitted Jacobian accumulates and saves in float32. Quantized fitting is not implemented.

fields.label: Python execution device
fields.help: cuda (or cuda:0) on the cluster, mps on a compatible Mac, or cpu for small numerical tests. The pilot must verify backward support on this architecture.

fields.label: Intended lens use
fields.help: testing for rehearsal, or evidence for intended study use. This declaration does not qualify the lens or validate a behavioral interpretation.

fields.label: Continue from a completed checkpoint (optional)
fields.help: Choose state.json beside sums.safetensors after the original job has stopped. Both files travel with the request and are read and verified again at execution; multi-gigabyte files can take several minutes. Continuation creates a new run. Numerical settings and dependency versions must match; documentation-only driver changes do not prevent continuation under the same fitting contract.

fields.label: Compile model blocks
fields.help: Optional speed experiment. Compare gradients and fitted lenses against the uncompiled baseline before using it for a longer run; first-call compilation counts in pilot time.

fields.label: Attention kernel selection
fields.help: current uses this prepared environment; torch explicitly selects inspectable Torch fallback functions. No packages are installed. Compare the two in a small benchmark before changing a continuation runtime.

fields.label: Optional stopping rule document
fields.help: JSON with threshold, window, and minPrompts. Stops after N consecutive available fitted-row changes below the threshold, after the minimum. Leave blank for a fixed row cap; sharded rounds remain fixed-budget.

fields.label: Advanced: explicit global row indices
fields.help: Usually generated by the round planner. Rows remain tied to the original corpus, allowing overlap checks at merge.

fields.label: Optional measured pilot report
fields.help: Choose benchmark-report.json from a matching model, corpus, and fitting configuration to display measured rows per hour and a cautious time extrapolation. This is not a walltime guarantee.

operations.claimBoundary: An averaged Jacobian is an instrument fitted to this corpus and runtime. Stable fitting statistics are not evidence of semantic validity or causal steering effects.
questions: What text population should the lens represent?
How will you assess readouts on held-out text after fitting?

operations.title: Compare fitting speed and numerical agreement
operations.purpose: Measure dimension batches, optional compilation, and prepared attention kernels on the same small text sample.

fields.label: Model to fit
fields.help: Choose a prepared Hugging Face checkpoint. Fitting does not download model weights or change them.

fields.label: Exact model version
fields.help: Inspect the model to pin its 40-character commit. The resulting lens belongs to this checkpoint.

fields.label: Published pilot fitting request
fields.help: Choose request.json from a fresh J-lens pilot with at most eight rows. Its corpus and preparation receipt travel with this benchmark.

fields.label: Dimension batches to compare
fields.help: Start with 1 as the reference. Each combination is a fresh worker; larger batches need more device memory.

fields.label: Kernel comparisons
fields.help: current benchmarks the prepared environment; torch uses the inspectable fallback; torch,current compares both. Installing kernels is a separate reviewed environment change.

fields.label: Also compare compiled blocks
fields.help: Doubles the number of cases. Includes first-call compilation in timing.

fields.label: Relative numerical tolerance
fields.help: Elementwise tolerance for per-prompt Jacobians and averaged lenses. Review the reported maximum and relative errors as well.

fields.label: Absolute numerical tolerance
fields.help: Absolute allowance near zero. This default is a comparison setting, not a claim of scientific adequacy.

operations.claimBoundary: Speed is conditional on these rows and this runtime. Agreement is measured with the displayed tolerances, not a universal scientific guarantee.
questions: Which small corpus should represent the later fitting workload?
Which numerical differences are acceptable for the intended analysis?

fields.help: Each shard retains its own lens and checkpoint, can be continued independently, and uses the same numerical settings.

fields.help: Set within the site’s policy. Queue top-ups count active scientific jobs on this controller and require an explicit review.
